ME-2024-LD836.aiSummary: Would authorize a $50 million state bond issue to help pay for upgrades to municipal culverts at stream crossings. The money would fund a competitive grant program that matches local funds for projects that improve fish and wildlife habitat and help towns prepare for floods and storms. Eligible applicants would include local governments, municipal conservation groups, soil and water conservation districts, and private nonprofit groups, and voters would have to approve the bond before it could take effect.

ME-2024-LD1888.aiSummary: This bill would create a new crime of racketeering in Maine. It would apply when a person is tied to a criminal group and takes part in at least two listed crimes, such as drug trafficking, human trafficking, theft, fraud, gambling, arson, or murder. It would also let the state seize assets linked to racketeering and set rules for where these cases can be brought. The bill is an emergency measure and would take effect when approved.

ME-2024-LD1639.policyArea: INSTRUCTIONAL HOURS, SCHOOL POLICIES, SCHOOL YEAR
ME-2024-LD1639.aiSummary: The bill would require each school in Maine to provide at least 900 instructional hours each school year, starting with the 2026-2027 school year. It defines instructional hours as regular school time for teaching and school-led learning, not lunch, recess, or after-school clubs, and it lets the education commissioner grant a waiver for emergencies like disasters or public health events. School units would also have to file yearly reports showing they meet the rule, and the state could take action if they do not.

ME-2024-LD1040.policyArea: BENEFITS CAP, STATE RETIREMENT SYSTEM, TEACHERS

The change would raise the amount of pension pay that can get the increase each year. It affects those retirees and their beneficiaries in Maine's state retirement system.
